Often with cystitis features (dysuria, frequency, urgency).
Nausea / vomiting, malaise.
Common organisms: E. coli (75 %), Klebsiella, Proteus, Enterococcus.
redFlags: Obstructive pyelonephritis (renal stone, prostate enlargement) — urgent imaging + decompression.
Diabetes — emphysematous pyelonephritis possible (gas in renal parenchyma) — emergency.
Renal abscess / perinephric abscess — drainage required.

diagnostics.rationale: WBC, nitrites, leucocyte esterase; culture > 10⁴ CFU/mL with relevant symptoms.
Positive 10–20 %; mandatory if sepsis features.
Severity + AKI.
Exclude obstruction (stone, hydronephrosis, abscess). Mandatory in pregnancy, diabetes, men, recurrent.
If obstruction suspected, complicated, no improvement at 48 h.

management.detail: Outpatient (uncomplicated): ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily orally for 7 days, OR cefalexin 1 g three times daily for 10–14 days. Pregnancy: IV ceftriaxone 1 g daily until afebrile + improving, then oral cefalexin for 10–14 days total. Sepsis / inpatient: IV ceftriaxone 1–2 g daily OR piperacillin-tazobactam.
IV crystalloid 30 mL/kg if septic / dehydrated. Antipyretic + antiemetic.
Obstructed pyelonephritis = SURGICAL EMERGENCY — urgent percutaneous nephrostomy OR retrograde stent. Antibiotic alone WILL NOT suffice.
Total 7 days (uncomplicated quinolone), 10–14 days (β-lactam or complicated). Switch to oral when stable + afebrile + tolerating PO.
Re-check urine culture 1–2 weeks post-treatment in pregnancy. Recurrent pyelonephritis → urology referral; investigate for stones, reflux, BPH.

title: Cryptococcal meningitis (adult)
presentation: Subacute headache (≥ 1 week), low-grade fever, malaise, in PLHIV with CD4 < 100.
Altered mental state, vomiting, neck stiffness (less prominent than bacterial).
Cranial nerve palsies (VI > VII > VIII).
Raised intracranial pressure prominent — visual loss, papilloedema, repeated vomiting.
Causes 15 % of HIV-related deaths globally; major SSA burden.
redFlags: Severely raised ICP (CSF opening pressure > 25 cmH₂O) → therapeutic LPs daily.
Cryptococcal IRIS (post-ART) — usually 1–4 weeks after ART initiation.
Sight-threatening papilloedema — emergency optic-nerve fenestration / shunt.

diagnostics.test: Cryptococcal antigen (CrAg) serum + CSF — preferred initial test
diagnostics.rationale: Lateral flow assay (CrAg LFA) — point-of-care, sensitivity > 95 %.
CSF: India ink (visualises encapsulated yeasts), culture (slow), CrAg, cell count (often subtle), protein, glucose.
PLHIV with CD4 < 100 is the at-risk population.

diagnostics.test: Brain CT before LP if focal signs / depressed consciousness / new seizure
diagnostics.rationale: Rule out mass / hydrocephalus.

management.detail: WHO 2022 preferred: single high-dose liposomal amphotericin B 10 mg/kg single dose + flucytosine 100 mg/kg/day in 4 doses × 14 days + fluconazole 1200 mg/day × 14 days (Ambition trial). Alternative: conventional amphotericin B 1 mg/kg/day + flucytosine × 7 days then fluconazole 1200 mg/day × 7 days.
Fluconazole 800 mg/day for 8 weeks.
Fluconazole 200 mg daily until CD4 > 200 sustained for 6 months on ART.
Daily LPs while CSF opening pressure > 25 cmH₂O — drain 20–30 mL or until pressure ≤ 20. CRITICAL — reduces mortality. Continue until ICP normalises (often 1–2 weeks).
DELAY ART for 4–6 weeks after starting antifungal therapy (COAT trial — early ART increases mortality from IRIS / direct neurotoxicity).
All PLHIV with CD4 < 200 — screen serum CrAg. If positive, asymptomatic: pre-emptive fluconazole 1200 mg/day × 2 weeks → consolidation → maintenance. Reduces incident meningitis by 60 %.

title: Bacterial vaginosis (BV)
presentation: Thin, homogeneous greyish-white vaginal discharge with characteristic fishy odour (worse after intercourse).
Vulval irritation NOT typical (distinguishes from candidiasis / trichomoniasis).
Frequently asymptomatic.
Mixed anaerobic overgrowth (Gardnerella, Atopobium, Prevotella, Mycoplasma hominis) replaces Lactobacillus.
redFlags: BV in pregnancy — associated with preterm birth, late miscarriage, PROM, postpartum endometritis.
Recurrent BV → screen STI panel + HIV / coexisting trichomoniasis.
BV + PID concurrent — atypical presentation; treat both.

diagnostics.test: Amsel criteria (3 of 4: thin homogeneous discharge, vaginal pH > 4.5, positive whiff test with 10 % KOH, > 20 % clue cells on saline microscopy)
diagnostics.rationale: Clinical bedside diagnosis.
Gold standard in research; ≥ 7 = BV.
Detects BV + Candida + Trichomonas simultaneously.

management.detail: Oral metronidazole 400 mg twice daily for 5–7 days. Alternative: 2 g single dose (less effective for recurrence). Or topical: metronidazole 0.75 % gel 5 g intravaginally daily × 5 days, OR clindamycin 2 % cream 5 g intravaginally at bedtime × 7 days.
Oral metronidazole 400 mg twice daily for 5–7 days. Treat symptomatic BV in pregnancy + asymptomatic with prior preterm birth (reduces preterm birth).

Avoid douching (perpetuates dysbiosis). Avoid alcohol during + 24 h after metronidazole (disulfiram-like). Counsel sex partners are NOT routinely treated (no significant reduction in recurrence). Same-sex female partners are sometimes co-treated.
Suppressive metronidazole 0.75 % gel 5 g intravaginally twice weekly for 4–6 months. Lactobacillus probiotic, boric-acid vaginal capsules adjunctive evidence.

title: Trichomoniasis (Trichomonas vaginalis)
presentation: Women: frothy yellow-green offensive vaginal discharge, vulvitis, dyspareunia, dysuria, strawberry cervix (rare but pathognomonic).
Men: urethritis (often asymptomatic — 70 %), occasionally epididymitis.
STI — sexually transmitted, frequently coexists with other STIs (gonorrhoea, chlamydia, syphilis, HIV).
redFlags: Trichomoniasis + HIV — increases HIV transmission + acquisition risk.
Pregnancy — associated with preterm birth + low birth weight + PROM.
Persistent infection despite metronidazole — consider higher-dose regimen, tinidazole, or NAAT-confirmed resistance.

diagnostics.rationale: Highest sensitivity > 95 %; on urine / vaginal / endocervical swab. Often multiplexed with chlamydia + gonorrhoea.
Motile trichomonads — sensitivity only 50 %, immediate result.
Suggestive but not specific (also BV).

diagnostics.test: Co-test HIV / syphilis / HBsAg / anti-HCV / chlamydia / gonorrhoea
diagnostics.rationale: Mandatory co-screening.

management.detail: Women: 500 mg twice daily for 7 days (preferred 2024 CDC update) OR 2 g single dose (lower cure rate). Men: 2 g single dose acceptable.
Tinidazole 2 g single dose — comparable cure, longer half-life.
Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days — safe in all trimesters. AVOID 2 g single dose in pregnancy (higher preterm-birth signal at high dose).
Concurrent treatment of all sexual partners from previous 60 days (expedited partner therapy where legal). Abstinence until 7 days after both partners treated AND symptoms resolved.
If symptoms persist 7 days after standard treatment: high-dose metronidazole 2 g daily for 5–7 days OR tinidazole 2 g daily for 5–7 days. Sensitivity testing if recurrent.
NAAT at 3 months — high re-infection rate.

title: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
presentation: New / worsening infiltrate on CXR + ≥ 2 of: fever > 38, leucocytosis / leucopenia, purulent secretions; in patient mechanically ventilated > 48 h.
Early-onset (< 5 days) — community-style organisms: S. pneumoniae, MSSA, H. influenzae.
Late-onset (≥ 5 days) — MDR pathogens: Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, ESBL Klebsiella, MRSA.
redFlags: Multidrug-resistant organism risk (recent broad-spectrum, prolonged ICU, ICU outbreak strain).
Bilateral cavitation — necrotising pneumonia, S. aureus pneumonia (post-influenza).

diagnostics.test: Endotracheal aspirate quantitative culture (≥ 10⁶ CFU/mL) OR bronchoalveolar lavage (≥ 10⁴ CFU/mL)
diagnostics.rationale: Distinguish colonisation from infection; guides de-escalation.
Yield ~ 15 %; mandatory in suspected VAP with sepsis.
New / worsening infiltrate.
Severity + de-escalation guidance.

management.step: Empirical antibiotics — early-onset, no MDR risk
management.detail: IV ceftriaxone 2 g daily OR piperacillin-tazobactam OR levofloxacin.

IV piperacillin-tazobactam OR meropenem (carbapenem if ESBL suspected) + amikacin / gentamicin (for double Gram-negative cover) + vancomycin / linezolid (MRSA cover). De-escalate at 48–72 h per cultures.
7 days for most VAP (shorter as effective as longer for non-fermenters). 14 days if S. aureus / Pseudomonas with poor response.
Head-of-bed elevation 30–45°. Oral chlorhexidine. Sedation interruption / spontaneous-breathing trials. Subglottic suctioning. Stress-ulcer prophylaxis. DVT prophylaxis.
Hand hygiene, daily sedation interruption, weaning protocol, oral chlorhexidine, head elevation, peptic ulcer + DVT prophylaxis — bundles reduce VAP rates 40–80 %.

title: Acute tonsillopharyngitis (adult / child)
presentation: Sore throat + erythematous pharynx / tonsils ± exudate / cervical lymphadenopathy / fever.
Most viral (> 80 %): rhinovirus, adenovirus, EBV (infectious mononucleosis), enterovirus.
Group A streptococcus (GAS) ~ 20–30 % in 5–15 y, ~ 10 % adults.
Centor / FeverPAIN scores stratify probability of GAS.
redFlags: Stridor, drooling, trismus, severe respiratory distress → epiglottitis / peritonsillar abscess / retropharyngeal abscess — emergency.
Suspected EBV — splenomegaly + atypical lymphocytes; AVOID amoxicillin (rash).
Post-streptococcal complications — acute rheumatic fever (1–3 weeks later), glomerulonephritis.

diagnostics.rationale: Stratify GAS probability. Score ≥ 3 — consider rapid antigen / antibiotic.

diagnostics.test: Rapid strep antigen test (RADT) ± throat culture
diagnostics.rationale: Specificity > 95 %; sensitivity 70–90 %. Useful where score 3–4.
Suspected infectious mononucleosis.

management.detail: Paracetamol + ibuprofen. Saltwater gargles, throat lozenges. Hydration. Reassure most pharyngitis is viral + self-limiting (resolves in 5–7 days).

Phenoxymethylpenicillin (penicillin V) 500 mg orally twice daily for 10 days. Penicillin allergy: clarithromycin 250 mg twice daily for 5 days OR azithromycin 500 mg once daily for 3 days. AVOID amoxicillin in suspected EBV (causes severe rash).
Delayed prescription strategy (collect in 3–5 days if not improving) — reduces antibiotic use without harm.
Tonsillectomy if ≥ 7 episodes / 1 year, ≥ 5 / year × 2 years, OR ≥ 3 / year × 3 years (Paradise criteria).
Severe unilateral pain + trismus + deviated uvula → ENT referral + IV antibiotics + needle aspiration / drainage.

references.label: NICE NG84 — Sore throat antimicrobial prescribing

title: Central-line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI)
presentation: Fever + sepsis features in patient with central venous catheter > 48 h with no other source.
May have signs at insertion site (erythema, purulence, tenderness) but often absent.
Common organisms: coagulase-negative staph (40 %), S. aureus, Candida, Gram-negative rods, Enterococcus.
redFlags: Septic shock from CLABSI — high mortality.
S. aureus / Candida / Pseudomonas bacteraemia — remove line, prolonged therapy.
Tunnel / port infection — visible along tunnel — line removal mandatory.
Septic thrombophlebitis — fever + persistent bacteraemia despite line removal + appropriate antibiotic.

diagnostics.test: Paired blood cultures (peripheral + each lumen of central line) BEFORE antibiotics
diagnostics.rationale: Differential time-to-positivity > 2 h favours line as source.
Roll plate ≥ 15 CFU/cm consistent with CLABSI.
S. aureus / Candida / Enterococcus bacteraemia — exclude endocarditis.

management.detail: IV vancomycin 15 mg/kg every 12 h (Gram+ cover) + piperacillin-tazobactam OR meropenem (Gram- cover). Add empirical antifungal (caspofungin / liposomal amphotericin) if septic shock, TPN, neutropenia, prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics, multi-site Candida colonisation.
REMOVE catheter if S. aureus, Candida, Pseudomonas, mycobacteria. Salvage attempt (line-lock therapy + IV antibiotic) acceptable for coag-neg staph in tunnelled long-term lines if no severe sepsis.
Targeted to organism: S. aureus 4–6 weeks IV. Candida 14 days after first negative culture + line removal. Gram-negative 7–14 days. Coag-neg staph 5–7 days.
Fluid resuscitation, vasopressor if shock, monitor end-organ function. Echo for S. aureus / Candida / Enterococcus (rule out endocarditis).

Chlorhexidine skin preparation, maximum sterile barriers at insertion, daily review of line necessity (remove ASAP), avoid femoral lines, scrub the hub before each access. Bundles reduce CLABSI by 60–80 %.

title: Genital herpes (HSV-1 / HSV-2)
presentation: First episode (primary): clusters of painful vesicles → ulcers on genital / perianal skin, fever, tender inguinal lymphadenopathy, dysuria.
Recurrent episodes: milder, shorter, often with prodromal tingling.
HSV-2 more recurrent (4–6 episodes / year); HSV-1 fewer recurrences.
Asymptomatic shedding common (responsible for most transmission).
redFlags: Pregnancy + primary HSV near term — high vertical transmission risk (30–50 %) → caesarean + IV aciclovir.
Severe / disseminated HSV in immunocompromised → IV aciclovir.

diagnostics.rationale: Gold standard — highest sensitivity; distinguishes HSV-1 vs HSV-2.
Lower sensitivity; useful where NAAT unavailable.
Establishes prior infection; differentiates HSV-1 vs HSV-2; useful in counselling. Not for screening asymptomatic.
Co-test STIs.

management.detail: Aciclovir 400 mg three times daily for 7–10 days OR valaciclovir 1 g twice daily for 7–10 days OR famciclovir 250 mg three times daily for 7–10 days. Start as early as possible — ideally within 72 h. Analgesia + topical anaesthetic (lidocaine gel). Saline baths. Hydration.

Episodic: 5-day course at first prodrome. Suppressive (preferred ≥ 6/year): aciclovir 400 mg twice daily, valaciclovir 500 mg once daily, famciclovir 250 mg twice daily — taken daily long-term. Reduces recurrences + asymptomatic shedding + transmission to partners by ~ 50 %.

First episode pregnancy: aciclovir 400 mg three times daily for 7–10 days. Suppressive aciclovir 400 mg three times daily from 36 weeks until delivery. Caesarean if primary infection / active lesions at onset of labour.
IV aciclovir 5–10 mg/kg every 8 h × 7–10 days. Switch to oral when improving.

Lifelong infection. Reduce transmission with consistent condom use, suppressive therapy, disclosure. Counsel triggers (stress, illness, immunosuppression). Notify regular partners — type-specific serology offered.

references.label: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines 2021 — Genital herpes

title: Infectious mononucleosis (EBV)
presentation: Triad: fever + sore throat + lymphadenopathy (cervical, posterior).
Malaise + fatigue often prolonged (weeks–months).
Splenomegaly 50 %, hepatomegaly 10 %.
Palatal petechiae common.
Maculopapular rash if given amoxicillin (~ 90 %).
redFlags: Splenic rupture (rare but life-threatening) — avoid contact sport + heavy lifting for ≥ 4 weeks.
Airway compromise from tonsillar enlargement — admit, consider corticosteroid.
Hepatitis — raised ALT 2–3× ULN; usually self-limiting.
Aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, encephalitis — rare but reported.

diagnostics.rationale: Quick bedside; sensitivity 85 % at week 2, lower in children < 5.
Confirmatory in monospot-negative or age < 5. Acute infection: VCA-IgM +, EBNA −.
Atypical lymphocytes (Downey cells) > 10 %.
Raised transaminases in 80 %.

management.detail: Rest, fluids, paracetamol + ibuprofen for fever and pain. Saline gargles, throat lozenges. Antiviral therapy NOT recommended (no benefit in immunocompetent).
Co-administration with EBV causes maculopapular rash in 80–90 % (not true allergy).
Avoid contact sport, heavy lifting, and vigorous exercise for at least 4 weeks (some recommend 8 weeks for athletes). Ultrasound to confirm spleen size if return to sport sooner.
Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day taper over 7 days ONLY for severe airway obstruction, severe haemolysis, neurologic complications. Not routine — may prolong viral shedding.
Fatigue lasts weeks–months; reassure. 9–12 % of cases develop post-viral chronic fatigue syndrome. Graduated return to activity.

title: Preterm labour + tocolysis
presentation: Regular uterine contractions (≥ 4 in 20 min) with cervical change at 24⁺⁰ – 36⁺⁶ weeks gestation.
Risk factors: previous preterm birth, multiple pregnancy, short cervix, infection (chorioamnionitis, UTI, BV), polyhydramnios, smoking.
redFlags: Suspected chorioamnionitis (fever + uterine tenderness + maternal / foetal tachycardia + offensive discharge) → DELIVER + IV antibiotics, do NOT tocolyse.
PROM > 18 h — limited benefit of tocolysis.

diagnostics.rationale: Cervical change, dilation, length < 15 mm. Avoid digital examination if PROM.
Negative test < 50 ng/mL has high NPV — preterm birth within 7 days unlikely.
Foetal well-being.

diagnostics.test: FBC, CRP, urinalysis + culture, vaginal swabs
diagnostics.rationale: Sepsis / UTI screen.

management.detail: Dexamethasone 6 mg IM every 12 h × 4 doses (24 mg total) OR betamethasone 12 mg IM every 24 h × 2 doses. Single course at 24⁺⁰–34⁺⁶ weeks. Repeat course only if > 7 days from first course AND < 32 weeks AND new high preterm-birth risk.
4 g IV loading over 20 min + 1 g/h infusion until birth or 24 h max, if < 32 weeks gestation. Reduces cerebral palsy by 30 %.

First-line nifedipine 20 mg orally, repeat at 30 min if contracting, then 10–20 mg orally every 4–8 h × 48 h. Alternative atosiban (oxytocin antagonist). Tocolysis buys 48 h for corticosteroids + transfer to higher-level unit.
Erythromycin 250 mg orally four times daily × 10 days (ORACLE 1). AVOID co-amoxiclav — necrotising-enterocolitis association in ORACLE 1.
In-utero transfer to facility with appropriate neonatal level (level 3 NICU if < 28 weeks).
IV benzylpenicillin 3 g loading + 1.5 g every 4 h until delivery; allergic — vancomycin or clindamycin.

references.label: WHO Recommendations on Preterm Birth Prevention 2022
ACOG Practice Bulletin — Management of Preterm Labour

title: Eclampsia — active seizure / immediate post-ictal management
presentation: Generalised tonic-clonic seizure in pregnancy / immediate postpartum (up to 6 weeks) without other cause.
Usually preceded by pre-eclampsia features (hypertension, proteinuria), severe headache, visual disturbance, RUQ pain, hyperreflexia.
30 % of eclampsia occurs without classic pre-eclampsia warning signs.
redFlags: Status eclampticus — repeated / continuous seizures despite MgSO₄.
Intracranial haemorrhage / PRES with focal signs — urgent CT.
Acute pulmonary oedema, HELLP, DIC, AKI.

diagnostics.rationale: Exclude alternative cause (hypoglycaemia, arrhythmia, sepsis).

diagnostics.test: FBC + LFT + U&E + coagulation + LDH + uric acid + urinalysis
diagnostics.rationale: HELLP screen, AKI, severity of pre-eclampsia.
Foetal well-being.
First-ever seizure OR focal signs OR atypical postnatal eclampsia — exclude haemorrhage / PRES / venous thrombosis.

management.detail: Left lateral recovery position. Oxygen 15 L non-rebreather. IV access × 2. Bite-block / suction. DO NOT force anything between teeth.

4 g IV in 20 mL 0.9 % NaCl over 5–10 min + 5 g IM into each buttock (with 1 % lidocaine). Maintenance: 5 g IM every 4 h for 24 h after seizure / delivery (whichever is later). Monitor RR ≥ 12, deep tendon reflexes present, urine output > 25 mL/h. Toxicity reversal: calcium gluconate 1 g IV.

Labetalol 20 mg IV repeat every 10 min, doubling dose (max 300 mg). OR hydralazine 5 mg IV every 20 min, max 20 mg. OR nifedipine 10 mg orally (NOT sublingual). Target 140–150 / 90–100 — do NOT lower below 140 (placental hypoperfusion).

Plan delivery once mother stabilised (BP controlled, no active seizure ≥ 1 h). Mode + timing depend on gestational age, parity, foetal status, urgency. Vaginal delivery often acceptable if stable + viable foetus.
Continue MgSO₄ (also serves as foetal neuroprotection if < 32 weeks). Dexamethasone if < 34 weeks AND delivery anticipated.

Continue MgSO₄ for 24 h after seizure. Strict fluid balance (max 80 mL/h — pulmonary oedema risk). Daily review of BP / labs / urine output. 25 % of eclampsia occurs postpartum — counsel return for warning signs up to 6 weeks.

title: Postpartum haemorrhage — active management + treatment
presentation: Blood loss ≥ 500 mL after vaginal delivery OR ≥ 1000 mL after caesarean OR clinical signs of hypovolaemia.
Primary PPH (≤ 24 h post-delivery) — most common; 4 Ts: Tone (uterine atony 80 %), Trauma (lacerations), Tissue (retained), Thrombin (coagulopathy).
Secondary PPH (24 h – 12 weeks) — retained products, endometritis, abnormal involution.
Risk: previous PPH, antepartum haemorrhage, prolonged labour, multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios, macrosomia, IOL, severe anaemia, instrumental delivery.
redFlags: Class III/IV shock (loss > 2 L) — pulseless, severe hypotension, altered mental state → MASSIVE TRANSFUSION protocol.
Concealed haemorrhage (uterine rupture, broad-ligament haematoma) — falsely low estimate.
Amniotic-fluid embolism / DIC — sudden cardiovascular collapse + bleeding from puncture sites + non-clotting blood.

diagnostics.test: Bedside obs + accurate quantitative blood loss measurement
diagnostics.rationale: Visual estimation underestimates by 30–50 %; use blood-soaked weigh / calibrated drape.

diagnostics.test: Bedside Hb, FBC, coagulation, fibrinogen, lactate, ABG
diagnostics.rationale: Severity + DIC screen. Fibrinogen < 2 g/L = severe, transfuse cryoprecipitate.

diagnostics.test: Cross-match 4 units packed red cells + 4 units FFP
diagnostics.rationale: Massive transfusion protocol — 1:1:1 RBC : FFP : platelet ratio.

management.detail: Two large-bore IV cannulae, oxygen 15 L, fluid resuscitation (warmed crystalloid 1 L bolus, repeat). Catheterise. Massive transfusion protocol if Class III/IV shock. Tilt left lateral if pregnant or recently postpartum.

(1) Bimanual uterine compression / massage. (2) IV oxytocin 10 IU bolus then 40 IU in 500 mL 0.9 % NaCl at 125 mL/h. (3) Add ergometrine 0.5 mg IV (AVOID in hypertension / pre-eclampsia). (4) Add carboprost (15-methyl PGF2α) 250 µg IM every 15 min, max 2 mg (AVOID in asthma). (5) Add misoprostol 800 µg sublingual / rectal. (6) Add tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 min within 3 h of bleeding onset (WOMAN trial; repeat 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 min).
Manual removal of retained placenta / products. IV ergometrine / oxytocin pre-procedure.
Speculum + manual exploration for vaginal / cervical / perineal lacerations. Suture with continuous-locking absorbable suture. Pack cervical / vaginal vault if oozing.
Transfuse 1:1:1 (packed cells : FFP : platelet). Cryoprecipitate / fibrinogen concentrate if fibrinogen < 2 g/L (< 3 g/L in HELLP / amniotic fluid embolism).

Intrauterine balloon tamponade (Bakri balloon) — 80 % effective for atony. If failed: B-Lynch / Hayman compression sutures, internal iliac / uterine artery ligation, arterial embolisation, peripartum hysterectomy. CEmONC facility transfer if required + safe.

title: Neonatal resuscitation (NRP / WHO HBB)
presentation: Newborn who is apnoeic, gasping, or has heart rate < 100 / min at birth.
Risk factors: prematurity, meconium-stained liquor, prolonged labour, abruption, cord prolapse, maternal infection, congenital malformation.
redFlags: HR < 60 despite effective ventilation → start chest compressions + adrenaline.
Persistent apnoea / cyanosis at 10 min → very poor prognosis; consider stopping if no signs of life at 20 min.
Severe meconium aspiration with HR < 100 → tracheal suction.
Diaphragmatic hernia / oesophageal atresia — abnormal abdomen / NG tube fails to pass.

diagnostics.rationale: Term? Tone? Breathing or crying?

diagnostics.test: HR + breathing every 30 sec during resuscitation
diagnostics.rationale: Guides escalation through NRP algorithm.
Target oxygen saturation: 1 min 60–65, 5 min 80–85, 10 min 85–95.

management.detail: Dry, warm (skin-to-skin or radiant warmer), position airway (neutral / sniffing), suction mouth then nose if obstructed, stimulate (rub back / flick foot).

If apnoeic / gasping / HR < 100 at 60 sec: 40–60 breaths/min via bag-mask + room air (21 % O₂ in term; 30 % preterm). Each breath ~ 1 s — see chest rise. Reassess HR + breathing at 30 sec. MR SOPA corrective steps if no chest rise: Mask reseat, Reposition, Suction, Open mouth, Pressure increase, Airway alternative (intubation / LMA).

If HR < 60 despite 30 sec of effective PPV: 3:1 compression-to-ventilation ratio (90 compressions + 30 breaths per minute = 120 events/min). Two-thumb encircling-hands technique preferred. Reassess HR at 60 sec.

If HR < 60 despite chest compressions + 100 % O₂: adrenaline 0.01–0.03 mg/kg (0.1–0.3 mL/kg of 1:10 000) IV / via umbilical-vein catheter, repeat every 3–5 min. Volume expansion: 10 mL/kg of 0.9 % NaCl over 5–10 min if hypovolaemia suspected (e.g. cord rupture, foetal-maternal haemorrhage).
Term infants ≥ 36 weeks with moderate / severe hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy: target rectal 33.0–34.0 °C for 72 h, started within 6 h of birth. Reduces death + disability.
Vitamin K 1 mg IM. Glucose check + correct < 2.6 mmol/L. Skin-to-skin / kangaroo mother care once stable. NICU admission for prolonged resuscitation / encephalopathy / preterm.

references.label: WHO Helping Babies Breathe (HBB) — Action Plan

title: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS)
presentation: Preterm newborn (< 34 weeks) with tachypnoea, grunting, nasal flaring, subcostal / intercostal recession, cyanosis within minutes / hours of birth.
Reduced air entry, fine crackles.
Most common cause of preterm respiratory distress; due to surfactant deficiency.
redFlags: Severe hypoxia (SpO₂ < 85 on room air, FiO₂ requirement > 0.40) — surfactant + advanced respiratory support.
Pneumothorax — sudden deterioration, asymmetric breath sounds, transillumination.
Failure of surfactant response → consider non-RDS cause (pneumonia, congenital heart disease, hernia).

diagnostics.rationale: Hypoinflation, reticulogranular ground-glass pattern, air bronchograms. Distinguish from pneumonia (asymmetric / focal), transient tachypnoea (fluid in fissures).
Respiratory acidosis + hypoxaemia.
Exclude congenital pneumonia (GBS, E. coli).
If considering pulmonary hypertension / congenital heart disease.

management.detail: Dexamethasone 6 mg IM × 4 doses OR betamethasone 12 mg IM × 2 doses to mother 24 weeks – 33⁺⁶ weeks if preterm delivery anticipated within 7 days. Reduces RDS by 50 %.
Nasal CPAP 5–7 cmH₂O initiated in delivery room — reduces need for ventilation + surfactant.

Poractant alfa 200 mg/kg via thin catheter during spontaneous CPAP breathing (less invasive surfactant administration — LISA) if FiO₂ > 0.30 in spontaneously breathing infant on CPAP. Alternative: INSURE (Intubation-Surfactant-Extubation). Repeat 100 mg/kg every 6–12 h if ongoing requirement, max 3 doses.

Mechanical ventilation if CPAP failure (apnoea, severe acidosis, FiO₂ > 0.40 persistent). Volume-targeted ventilation reduces broncho-pulmonary dysplasia vs pressure-controlled. Target tidal volume 4–6 mL/kg. PEEP 5–8 cmH₂O. Permissive hypercapnia (PaCO₂ 45–55 mmHg) reduces lung injury.

Thermoregulation (warmer / kangaroo where possible), IV 10 % dextrose 60–80 mL/kg/day on day 1, advance to total fluids 150 mL/kg/day; minimal handling, parenteral nutrition by day 2–3. Empirical antibiotics (ampicillin + gentamicin) for 48 h until culture-negative.
Wean FiO₂ → CPAP → high-flow → room air. Caffeine citrate 20 mg/kg loading + 5–10 mg/kg/day — facilitates extubation + reduces BPD.

title: Ectopic pregnancy
presentation: Classic triad (only 50 %): amenorrhoea (6–8 weeks), abdominal / pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding.
Shoulder-tip pain (diaphragmatic irritation from haemoperitoneum).
Atypical: dizziness, syncope, GI upset, urinary symptoms.
Risk: previous ectopic, tubal surgery / disease, PID history, IUD in situ, IVF, smoking, age > 35.
redFlags: Ruptured ectopic — haemodynamic instability (tachycardia + hypotension + peritonism) → SURGICAL EMERGENCY.
Heterotopic pregnancy (intrauterine + ectopic) — possible with IVF; cannot exclude even with confirmed IUP on scan.
Cervical / interstitial / scar / ovarian ectopic — atypical sites, higher risk.

diagnostics.rationale: Discriminatory zone — ≥ 1500 IU/L should show intrauterine gestation on TVS. Slow rise (< 35 % over 48 h) suggests non-viable / ectopic.
Definitive — extrauterine gestation, free fluid, empty uterus with raised β-hCG.
Severity + transfusion preparation.

management.detail: Indicated for ruptured / haemodynamically unstable / non-compliant patient. Salpingectomy (removal of tube) for damaged tube + contralateral healthy tube. Salpingostomy (preservation) if contralateral tube absent / abnormal — but 15 % require further treatment for persistent trophoblast.

ELIGIBILITY: haemodynamically stable + β-hCG < 5000 IU/L + ectopic mass < 35 mm + no foetal cardiac activity + no contraindication. Dose: 50 mg/m² IM single dose. Re-check β-hCG day 4 + 7 (expect ≥ 15 % fall day 4 → 7). 14 % require second dose; 7 % surgical rescue. Counsel — avoid pregnancy + folic acid + alcohol + NSAIDs for 3 months.
Highly selected — β-hCG < 1000 + falling, asymptomatic + reliable follow-up. β-hCG twice-weekly until < 5 IU/L. Failure → medical / surgical.
Anti-D immunoglobulin 250 IU IM if Rh-negative woman. Psychological support — pregnancy loss is significant; offer counselling + contraception.
75 % conceive naturally afterwards. Recurrence risk 10 %. Early scan in next pregnancy at 6 weeks. Tobacco cessation. Chlamydia screen.

title: Miscarriage / early pregnancy loss
presentation: Vaginal bleeding ± abdominal pain at < 20 weeks gestation. ~ 15 % of clinically recognised pregnancies.
Threatened (bleeding, closed os, viable pregnancy on scan).
Inevitable (bleeding, open cervix).
Incomplete (passed some products, open os, retained tissue).
Complete (passed all products, closed os, empty uterus on scan).
Missed (failed pregnancy without bleeding; gestational sac without foetus / no foetal cardiac activity on scan).
redFlags: Heavy bleeding + haemodynamic instability — surgical evacuation + IV fluids + transfusion.
Septic miscarriage (fever, offensive discharge, abdominal pain) — IV antibiotics + urgent evacuation.
Recurrent miscarriage (≥ 3 consecutive) — workup for thrombophilia, antiphospholipid syndrome, uterine anomaly, parental karyotype.

diagnostics.rationale: Confirm gestational sac, foetal pole, cardiac activity, retained products. Diagnose missed miscarriage (CRL ≥ 7 mm without cardiac activity OR sac ≥ 25 mm without foetal pole).
Falling > 50 % over 48 h with empty uterus = complete miscarriage. Rising / static — exclude ectopic.
Anti-D need.
FBC, CRP, blood + endometrial culture.

management.detail: Wait up to 2 weeks for spontaneous completion; safe in haemodynamically stable woman without sepsis. Daily-emergency-bag-ready advice. Repeat scan at 2 weeks → complete (no further action) OR ongoing retained → medical / surgical.

Misoprostol 800 µg vaginal OR 600 µg buccal / sublingual, single dose. Counsel cramping + bleeding (8–14 days). 85 % completion rate; repeat if not completed. Add mifepristone 200 mg orally 24 h before misoprostol — increases success (NEJM 2018).

Suction curettage or manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for: heavy bleeding, infection, missed miscarriage with patient preference, failed medical. Avoid cervical dilation > 12 mm to reduce damage. Antibiotic prophylaxis (doxycycline 200 mg single dose).
Anti-D 250 IU IM for Rh-negative women at any miscarriage from 12 weeks; below 12 weeks if surgical evacuation / heavy bleeding. Psychological support — pregnancy loss is significant grief.

≥ 3 first-trimester OR ≥ 1 second-trimester losses. Investigate: parental karyotype, thrombophilia screen + antiphospholipid antibodies, uterine anomaly (3D-USS or HSG), TSH + glucose. Treat antiphospholipid syndrome with aspirin 75 mg + LMWH; otherwise reassure + supportive care.
Pregnancy test 3 weeks after — should be negative. Discuss future pregnancy planning, folic acid 400 µg pre-conception (5 mg if obese / diabetic / previous NTD).

title: Medical termination of pregnancy (MTOP, ≤ 12 weeks)
presentation: Woman seeking termination of pregnancy within first trimester (≤ 12⁺⁶ weeks) per WHO / local law.
Counsel on options (medical vs surgical), success rates, side effects, follow-up requirements.
Confirm dating by LMP + bedside ultrasound. Exclude ectopic.
redFlags: Suspected ectopic pregnancy — DO NOT proceed with MTOP until ectopic excluded.
Severe ongoing bleeding / sepsis from incomplete MTOP — surgical evacuation.
Rare Clostridium sordellii sepsis after misoprostol (4–7 days post — fever, severe abdominal pain, tachycardia).

diagnostics.rationale: Determines regimen (≤ 9 vs 9–12 weeks) and excludes ectopic.
Anti-D + baseline.

diagnostics.test: STI screen — chlamydia, gonorrhoea, HIV, syphilis
diagnostics.rationale: Test + treat before / at procedure; reduces post-procedure PID.

management.detail: Mifepristone 200 mg orally, followed 24–48 h later by misoprostol 800 µg buccal / sublingual / vaginal. Single misoprostol dose effective in 95 %; second 400 µg sublingual at 4 h if no bleeding. Take antiemetic + analgesic 30 min pre-misoprostol.
Mifepristone 200 mg → 36–48 h later misoprostol 800 µg vaginal then 400 µg every 3 h up to 4 additional doses.
Ibuprofen 400 mg 4-hourly + paracetamol 1 g 6-hourly. Heat pack. Counsel cramping (worse than menses), heavy bleeding (8–14 days), passage of clots / tissue.
Anti-D 250 IU IM for Rh-negative women ≥ 10 weeks. Discuss contraception — can start immediately post-procedure (COC / DMPA / LARC). IUD insertion can occur at the time of the procedure.
Self-test home urine pregnancy in 3 weeks (should be negative) OR clinic review at 14 days with serum β-hCG (expect 80 % decline). Ultrasound if uncertain. ~ 3 % require surgical evacuation.
Sensitive non-judgemental counselling. Document consent + capacity. Sexual / reproductive health support. Mental-health screening — counselling support offered.

title: Emergency contraception — counselling + provision
presentation: Unprotected sex / contraceptive failure (missed pill, condom break, late injection, sexual assault) within last 5 days.
Counsel as soon as possible — sooner = more effective.
Risk assessment: timing, BMI, current medications, contraceptive history.
redFlags: Established pregnancy (positive test before EC) — EC not effective; offer MTOP discussion.
Sexual assault — safeguard, STI screen + prophylaxis, mental-health support, police referral if patient willing.

diagnostics.rationale: Exclude established pregnancy before EC.
Timing, BMI, current contraception, allergies, medications (CYP3A4 inducers).

management.detail: Insert within 5 days of unprotected sex OR 5 days of earliest predicted ovulation. Failure rate < 0.1 %. Effective regardless of BMI / enzyme inducers. Acts as immediate ongoing contraception. Screen + treat / cover STI.

management.step: Ulipristal acetate (UPA) 30 mg orally — within 120 h
management.detail: Failure rate ~ 1.4 %. More effective than LNG, especially mid-cycle. AVOID concurrent oestrogen-based contraception × 5 days. Delays hormonal contraception start by 5 days. AVOID in severe asthma, hepatic impairment. Less effective if BMI > 35 (limited evidence).
Failure rate ~ 2 %. Decreasing efficacy with time. DOUBLE-DOSE 3 mg if BMI > 26 or weight > 70 kg. AVOID in enzyme inducer use (carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenytoin) — use Cu-IUD instead.
Start regular hormonal contraception same day as LNG; wait 5 days after UPA. Use condoms / additional precaution for first 7–9 days of restart.
Pregnancy test if menses delayed > 7 days. STI screen at 2 weeks (chlamydia / gonorrhoea NAAT) + 3 months (HIV / syphilis). Long-term contraception plan.

title: Opioid use disorder — treatment (OAT)
presentation: DSM-5 / ICD-11 substance-use disorder criteria — tolerance, withdrawal, craving, use despite harm, time spent, social impairment.
Withdrawal: yawning, lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, sweating, piloerection, dilated pupils, mild fever, anxiety, GI upset, myalgia, restlessness.
Heroin / illicit fentanyl / prescription opioid origins. Increasing rates globally including SSA.
redFlags: Pregnancy + opioid use — risk of neonatal abstinence syndrome.
HIV / HCV / HBV screening — high prevalence with IVDU.

diagnostics.rationale: Objective severity score — guides OAT initiation timing (COWS ≥ 12 for buprenorphine to avoid precipitated withdrawal).
Confirms opioid use, identifies polysubstance use.

diagnostics.test: HIV / HBV / HCV / syphilis + TB screen
diagnostics.rationale: Co-screen mandatory; high prevalence in IVDU.
QTc baseline + screening for methadone > 100 mg.
Co-morbidity + pregnancy planning.

management.detail: Non-judgemental. Naloxone take-home kit + family training. Safe-injection counselling (sterile equipment, do not share). Hepatitis vaccination. Refer to peer-support / community service.

management.step: Opioid agonist therapy (OAT) — METHADONE or BUPRENORPHINE
management.detail: First-line evidence-based intervention. Reduces overdose death, IDU, HIV transmission, crime. Methadone better retention; buprenorphine safer. Long-term — typically months to years; some lifelong. Daily-supervised dispensing first 3 months.

10–30 mg orally on day 1 (lower if low tolerance). Titrate 5–10 mg every 3–5 days to effective dose (typically 60–120 mg). Counsel: respiratory depression in first week (long t½). ECG baseline + 30 days.

Must wait until objective withdrawal (COWS ≥ 12) — ~ 12–24 h after last short-acting opioid, 36–48 h after methadone. Start 4 mg sublingual; second 4 mg dose 2–4 h later if withdrawal persists. Titrate to 8–16 mg/day. Suboxone (with naloxone) preferred to deter injection.
After 7+ days opioid-free → naltrexone 50 mg daily OR depot 380 mg IM monthly. RELAPSE-DEATH risk after detox due to lost tolerance — counsel intensively. Concurrent psychosocial support essential.

Continue / start OAT during pregnancy. Methadone or buprenorphine both acceptable (MOTHER trial — buprenorphine less neonatal abstinence severity). AVOID detoxification in pregnancy (relapse + overdose risk).
CBT, motivational interviewing, contingency management. Treat depression / anxiety / PTSD. Stable housing + employment support. Long-term remission rates 40–60 % with comprehensive treatment.

references.label: WHO Pharmacological Treatment of Opioid Dependence
NICE CG52 — Drug misuse — opioid detoxification

title: Alcohol use disorder — treatment + withdrawal management
presentation: DSM-5 / ICD-11 substance-use disorder criteria.
Withdrawal (6–48 h after last drink): tremor, anxiety, sweating, GI upset, insomnia. Severe: seizures (12–48 h), delirium tremens (48–96 h: confusion, autonomic instability, hallucinations).
Comorbidities: liver disease (60 % cirrhosis at 20 years dependence), pancreatitis, Wernicke-Korsakoff, peripheral neuropathy, depression, suicide.
redFlags: Delirium tremens — life-threatening (5 % mortality with treatment, 35 % without).
Wernicke encephalopathy — confusion + ataxia + ophthalmoplegia → IV thiamine.

diagnostics.rationale: Validated screening; AUDIT ≥ 8 (men) / ≥ 7 (women) = risk; AUDIT ≥ 20 = likely dependence.

diagnostics.test: Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol (CIWA-Ar)
diagnostics.rationale: Severity scoring — guides benzodiazepine dosing during withdrawal.

diagnostics.test: FBC + LFT + U&E + glucose + INR + clotting + γGT + MCV
diagnostics.rationale: Liver dysfunction, electrolyte disturbance, anaemia.

diagnostics.test: Vitamin B12, folate, magnesium, thiamine (or empirically replace)
diagnostics.rationale: Micronutrient deficiency common.
Cardiac comorbidity, alcohol cardiomyopathy.

management.detail: Admit if CIWA > 15, history of withdrawal seizures / DT, comorbidity. Chlordiazepoxide 30–40 mg orally every 6 h on day 1, taper over 7–10 days. CIWA-Ar guided dosing. IV thiamine 500 mg three times daily for 3 days (Pabrinex) BEFORE any glucose (Wernicke prevention). Multivitamins + electrolyte correction.

ICU. IV diazepam / lorazepam — escalating doses titrated to control. IV thiamine 500 mg three times daily for 3 days. Haloperidol 2.5–5 mg IV / IM PRN for hallucinations (caution — lowers seizure threshold). Aggressive hydration + electrolyte correction. Mortality 5 %.

Naltrexone 50 mg daily (best evidence; first-line). Acamprosate 666 mg three times daily (alternative; particularly useful for sustained abstinence). Disulfiram 200 mg daily (aversive — produces severe reaction on alcohol consumption — supervised; not first-line).
Cognitive behavioural therapy, motivational interviewing, mutual-help groups (AA, SMART Recovery), residential rehabilitation, contingency management. Treat co-morbid depression / anxiety / PTSD.
Hepatology referral for liver disease. FibroScan / abdominal USS surveillance. Nutritional support — protein-rich diet. Long-term thiamine 100 mg daily.

Total abstinence advised. Screen all pregnant women with AUDIT-C. Tapered detoxification under specialist; benzodiazepines used cautiously. Foetal alcohol-spectrum disorder counselling. Long-term + multidisciplinary support.

references.label: NICE CG115 — Alcohol-use disorders: diagnosis + clinical management

title: Tobacco use cessation
presentation: Smoking history (current / ex-smoker, pack-years), motivation to quit (5 As — Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, Arrange).
Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence — guides intensity of intervention.
Comorbidities: CV disease, COPD, lung cancer, malignancies, periodontal disease, pregnancy complications.
redFlags: Cardiac event in patient who continues smoking — cessation reduces re-infarction by 50 %.
Severe COPD / lung cancer — counsel risk + benefit; quitting reduces mortality at any age.
Pregnancy — preterm birth, IUGR, abruption, stillbirth, SIDS risk.

diagnostics.rationale: Brief intervention; ≥ 50 % of cessation attempts originate from healthcare encounter.
Severity guides pharmacotherapy intensity.
Objective marker of recent smoking; useful feedback tool.

management.detail: Individual / group counselling, motivational interviewing, telephone quitline, mobile apps, NHS Stop-Smoking Service / equivalent. Effectiveness doubles with structured support.

Combination NRT most effective (patch + acute formulation). Patch: 21 mg daily (high-dependence), 14 mg (moderate), 7 mg (low) for 8–12 weeks. Add lozenge / gum / inhaler / nasal spray for breakthrough cravings. Safe in pregnancy.

Partial nicotinic-receptor agonist. Start 0.5 mg daily × 3 days → 0.5 mg twice daily × 4 days → 1 mg twice daily for 12 weeks (longer 24 weeks if continued benefit). 25–35 % long-term abstinence at 1 year. Counsel rare neuropsychiatric effects (mood change, vivid dreams) — improved evidence shows no increased suicidality.

Atypical antidepressant. 150 mg daily × 3 days → 150 mg twice daily for 7–12 weeks. Less effective than varenicline. Avoid in seizure disorder, eating disorder, bipolar disorder, severe hepatic impairment.

Emerging evidence: more effective than NRT alone for cessation in some studies. NICE / RCP recommend offering as adjunct in motivated smokers who have failed NRT. NOT for never-smokers or adolescents. Long-term harms uncertain.

Behavioural support first-line. NRT (intermittent formulations preferred — patches removed at bedtime) if behavioural alone insufficient. AVOID varenicline + bupropion in pregnancy (limited safety data).
Most relapse within first 3 months — emphasise this is a chronic relapsing condition, not failure. Each quit attempt brings closer to permanent cessation. Re-offer after each relapse.

references.label: NICE NG209 — Tobacco: preventing uptake, promoting quitting

title: Severe acute malnutrition — inpatient stabilisation (child)
presentation: Severe wasting (MUAC < 115 mm or weight-for-height < −3 Z) OR bilateral pitting oedema OR weight-for-height < −3 Z.
Admission criteria (WHO IMAM): SAM with medical complication (anorexia + danger signs / severe oedema / IMCI danger sign / dehydration / hypothermia / hypoglycaemia / pneumonia).
redFlags: Severe hypoglycaemia (< 3 mmol/L) → immediate 10 % dextrose 5 mL/kg.
Severe shock — cautious fluid (10–15 mL/kg over 1 h ONLY if severe + cardiac monitor), risk of fluid-overload + heart failure.

diagnostics.rationale: Confirm SAM classification.
Stabilisation parameters.

diagnostics.test: Sepsis screen — blood + urine + stool culture
diagnostics.rationale: Subtle / non-classic infection presentation.

diagnostics.test: HIV test, malaria smear, TB screen
diagnostics.rationale: Underlying contributors common in SSA.

management.detail: (1) Prevent / treat hypoglycaemia — 10 % dextrose 5 mL/kg + start F-75 feeds every 2 h. (2) Prevent / treat hypothermia — warm wraps + heating. (3) Cautious rehydration — ReSoMal (low-sodium ORS) 5 mL/kg every 30 min × 2 h then 5–10 mL/kg/h alternate-hourly with F-75. AVOID IV fluids unless severe shock. (4) Correct electrolytes — extra potassium 3–4 mmol/kg/day + magnesium 0.4–0.6 mmol/kg/day. AVOID iron initially. (5) Treat infection — empirical amoxicillin 25 mg/kg every 8 h × 5 days (mild) OR ampicillin + gentamicin (severe). (6) Correct micronutrients — vitamin A 50 000–200 000 IU oral on day 1, folic acid 5 mg, multivitamin.
F-75 formula 130 mL/kg/day in 8–12 feeds, every 2–3 h day + night. Cup or NG if unable to drink. Aim 100 kcal/kg/day. Do NOT push weight gain in stabilisation phase.

Transition from F-75 to F-100 (130 kcal/kg/day) once appetite returns + oedema gone. Up to 200 kcal/kg/day for catch-up growth. Add iron 3 mg/kg/day after stabilisation (day 7). Develop sensory + emotional stimulation programme.

Weight-for-height ≥ −2 Z (or > 90 % of median), no oedema for 14 days, complications resolved, appetite test passed, primary caregiver trained. Transfer to outpatient therapeutic programme (OTP) with ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF).
Weekly weight + MUAC + oedema check until discharge. Sustained-recovery monitoring 6 months. Address underlying cause — food security, breastfeeding support, HIV ART, TB treatment, family planning.

references.label: WHO Inpatient Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition

title: Neonatal hypoglycaemia
presentation: Often asymptomatic (especially preterm / SGA). Screened at 1–4 h of life in at-risk infants.
Symptomatic: jitteriness, tremor, hypotonia, apnoea, poor feeding, lethargy, hypothermia, cyanosis, seizures.
Thresholds (WHO / AAP): operational threshold < 2.6 mmol/L (47 mg/dL); transient asymptomatic < 1.4 mmol/L in first 4 h acceptable in healthy term.
Risk: preterm, SGA, LGA, infant of diabetic mother, hypothermia, sepsis, perinatal asphyxia, beta-blocker maternal use.
redFlags: Hypoglycaemia + seizure / altered mental state → IV glucose + workup.
Persistent hypoglycaemia > 48 h → investigate for endocrine / metabolic cause (hyperinsulinism, growth-hormone deficiency, panhypopituitarism, inborn errors of metabolism).
Maternal diabetes — particular risk first 24 h.

diagnostics.rationale: Confirm; check 30 min after feed or every 3 h in at-risk.

diagnostics.test: If persistent — critical sample at hypoglycaemia: serum glucose + insulin + C-peptide + cortisol + GH + ketones + ammonia + lactate + plasma amino acids + urinary organic acids
diagnostics.rationale: Diagnose hyperinsulinism, hormone deficiency, IEM.

management.detail: Breastfeed immediately (or expressed breast milk / donor milk / formula 40 mL/kg/day in 8 feeds). Skin-to-skin care + warmth. Recheck glucose 30 min after feed.

management.step: Asymptomatic moderate 1.5–2.5 mmol/L OR symptomatic any level
management.detail: Buccal dextrose-gel 40 % 0.5 mL/kg + breastfeed (Sugar Babies Trial — reduces NICU admission by 50 %).

management.step: Severe < 1.5 mmol/L OR symptomatic OR repeat failure
management.detail: IV 10 % dextrose 2 mL/kg bolus over 2–3 min. Follow with 10 % dextrose infusion at 60–80 mL/kg/day (= ~ 5–7 mg/kg/min glucose). Recheck glucose at 15 + 30 min. Increase infusion concentration / rate (max 8–10 mg/kg/min in newborn) if persistent.
Critical sample BEFORE bolus. If hyperinsulinism suspected: diazoxide 5–15 mg/kg/day + chlorothiazide. If panhypopituitarism: hydrocortisone 1 mg/kg every 6 h. If IEM: stop feeds + specialist.
Early skin-to-skin + breastfeeding within 1 h of birth. Pre-feed glucose at 1, 2, 4 h then every 3 h in infants of diabetic mother / preterm / SGA / LGA until 3 stable values > 2.6.

title: Acute asthma exacerbation — paediatric (1–11 years)
presentation: Cough, wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness — often viral-triggered.
Severity (BTS / GINA): moderate (SpO₂ ≥ 92, able to talk, HR < 140/min 2–5 y or < 125/min ≥ 5 y, RR < 40 2–5 y or < 30 ≥ 5 y, PEF > 50 % best/predicted).
Severe: SpO₂ < 92, unable to complete sentences / feed, HR ≥ 140 or ≥ 125, RR ≥ 40 or ≥ 30, PEF 33–50 %.
Life-threatening: silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, confusion, PEF < 33 %, SpO₂ < 92 despite oxygen + treatment.
redFlags: Silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, altered mental state, PEF < 33 % → life-threatening; PICU.
Prior near-fatal asthma / ICU admission / intubation — highest-risk patient.

diagnostics.rationale: Drives immediate management decisions.
SpO₂ < 92 = severe.
Severity + treatment response.

diagnostics.test: CXR — only if pneumothorax suspected or atypical course
diagnostics.rationale: Not routinely required.
PaCO₂ rising / normalising is ominous (fatigue).

management.detail: Salbutamol 4–10 puffs via spacer + mask (use spacer NOT nebuliser as first-line per GINA — equally effective + fewer side effects). Repeat every 20 min × 3 if needed. Add oral prednisolone 1–2 mg/kg (max 40 mg, 3-day course; up to 5 days if not improving).

Oxygen target SpO₂ 94–98 %. Nebulised salbutamol 2.5 mg (< 5 y) or 5 mg (≥ 5 y) + ipratropium 250 µg, repeat every 20 min × 3. Oral prednisolone 1–2 mg/kg OR IV methylprednisolone 1–2 mg/kg if vomiting. Admit.

Continuous nebulised salbutamol + ipratropium. IV magnesium sulphate 40 mg/kg (max 2 g) over 20 min. IV salbutamol 15 µg/kg single bolus then 1–5 µg/kg/min infusion (cardiac monitor). IV hydrocortisone 4 mg/kg every 6 h. ICU + advanced airway team standby. Aminophylline 5 mg/kg loading + 1 mg/kg/h infusion specialist.

SpO₂ ≥ 95 on room air, no recession, normal HR / RR for age, taking PO + bronchodilator > 4-hourly intervals. Complete steroid course (3–5 days). Updated asthma action plan + inhaler-technique check. Smoking-exposure cessation counselling. Follow-up within 1 week with primary care + chase-up call at 48 h.

management.step: Prevent next attack — review GINA controller
management.detail: After any moderate / severe attack, review and STEP UP controller therapy (start ICS if not on; increase dose if on). Identify triggers, check inhaler technique, address adherence.

title: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar)
presentation: Prolonged fever (> 2 weeks) — typically afebrile pattern
Massive splenomegaly + hepatomegaly
Pancytopenia (anaemia + leucopenia + thrombocytopenia)
Weight loss + cachexia + darkening of skin (kala-azar = 'black sickness')
Endemic foci: South Sudan, Ethiopia, Sudan, Kenya, Uganda, Somalia

diagnostics.rationale: sensitivity > 95 % East African, lower (~85 %) in Sudan/Ethiopia
gold standard; bone marrow safer than splenic

diagnostics.test: FBC + LFTs + creatinine + albumin + HIV test
diagnostics.rationale: screen for HIV co-infection + baseline before antimonials

management.detail: rK39 + clinical or parasitological confirmation before treatment.
Combination — sodium stibogluconate 20 mg/kg/day IM + paromomycin 15 mg/kg IM × 17 days OR miltefosine 2.5 mg/kg/day PO + paromomycin × 10 days.
Liposomal amphotericin B 30–40 mg/kg total dose over 6 days + maintenance therapy + ART optimisation.
Weekly ECG, LFTs, amylase, FBC on stibogluconate. Test of cure at 6 + 12 months (clinical + spleen size).
Notify NTD focal point; sandfly vector control + case finding.

title: Cutaneous leishmaniasis
presentation: Painless skin nodule → ulcer with raised indurated edge + central crust
Often on exposed skin (face, arms, legs)
Persists for weeks–months; lymphadenitis may precede lesion
Mucosal involvement (rare in Africa; suggests L. tropica / L. major) → nasal / oral destruction

diagnostics.test: Lesion smear + Giemsa — amastigotes in macrophages
diagnostics.rationale: first-line diagnostic
guides therapy + epidemiology

management.step: Simple Old-World CL (single lesion, no mucosal risk)
management.detail: Local therapy — intralesional sodium stibogluconate + thermotherapy / cryotherapy OR topical paromomycin.

management.step: Complex CL or risk of dissemination
management.detail: Systemic — sodium stibogluconate 20 mg/kg/day IM × 20 days OR miltefosine 2.5 mg/kg/day PO × 28 days OR liposomal amphotericin B.
Systemic liposomal amphotericin B + extended duration; consider secondary prophylaxis.

title: African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness)
presentation: Stage 1 (haemolymphatic): chancre at tsetse bite, intermittent fever, lymphadenopathy (posterior cervical = Winterbottom sign), pruritus
Stage 2 (meningoencephalitic): sleep–wake reversal, behavioural change, confusion, tremor, ataxia → coma + death untreated
T.b. gambiense (West/Central Africa, chronic) vs T.b. rhodesiense (East/South Africa, acute)

diagnostics.test: CATT (Card Agglutination Test for Trypanosomiasis) — gambiense
diagnostics.rationale: field screening

diagnostics.test: Wet blood film / lymph aspirate / thick blood smear
diagnostics.rationale: demonstrate trypanosomes

diagnostics.test: LP — CSF cell count + trypanosomes + IgM
diagnostics.rationale: stage 1 vs 2 determination (CSF WBC > 5/µL or trypanosomes = stage 2)

management.detail: Fexinidazole 1800 mg/day × 4 days then 1200 mg/day × 6 days (with food).
Nifurtimox-eflornithine combination therapy (NECT): eflornithine 400 mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses × 7 days + nifurtimox 15 mg/kg/day PO × 10 days.
Stage 1: suramin (specialist supply). Stage 2: melarsoprol — high CNS toxicity, used only when no alternative.
WHO-mandated notification. Tsetse vector control.

title: Onchocerciasis (river blindness)
presentation: Chronic itching + papular dermatitis (onchodermatitis)
Subcutaneous nodules (onchocercomata) over bony prominences
Visual impairment: punctate keratitis → sclerosing keratitis + iridocyclitis + optic nerve atrophy → blindness
Endemic: river-blackfly zones in West + Central Africa (Volta basin, Lake Victoria)
redFlags: Loa loa co-endemicity — risk of encephalopathy on ivermectin

diagnostics.test: Skin snip — microfilariae visible under microscope
diagnostics.rationale: definitive
DEC patch test — risk of severe reaction
ocular disease

diagnostics.test: Loa loa screen in West/Central Africa
diagnostics.rationale: before ivermectin in endemic regions

management.detail: Ivermectin 150 µg/kg PO single dose — repeat every 6–12 months × several years (kills microfilariae; adults survive).
If Loa loa microfilarial load > 8000/mL, use alternative (doxycycline 100 mg/day × 6 weeks — kills Wolbachia → sterilises adults) OR hospitalise during ivermectin.
Community-directed ivermectin annually in endemic communities; coordinated with APOC / ESPEN.
Refer to ophthalmology for monitoring + surgical removal of corneal microfilariae if possible.

title: Lymphatic filariasis
presentation: Acute filarial lymphangitis (fever + tender lymphatics)
Chronic lymphoedema + elephantiasis (lower limb, genital — hydrocoele)
Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia (paroxysmal nocturnal cough)
Endemic: 'belt of LF' across SSA + South Asia
redFlags: Co-infection with onchocerciasis or Loa loa

diagnostics.rationale: fingertip rapid test, day or night sample
10 PM–2 AM peak (Wuchereria nocturnal periodicity)

diagnostics.test: Ultrasound — adult worm 'filaria dance sign' in scrotal lymphatics
diagnostics.rationale: in male patients with hydrocoele

management.detail: Single dose IDA: ivermectin 200 µg/kg + DEC 6 mg/kg + albendazole 400 mg.
Use DEC + albendazole (DEC alternative) OR DOXYCYCLINE 200 mg/day × 6 weeks (anti-Wolbachia).
Hygiene — soap + water + elevation + bandaging; treat ADLA episodes with antibiotics; surgery for hydrocoele.
Annual community treatment in endemic districts until prevalence < 1 % for 5 years.

title: Leprosy (Hansen disease)
presentation: Hypopigmented or erythematous skin patches with sensory loss
Enlarged peripheral nerves (ulnar, common peroneal, great auricular)
Motor + sensory deficits — claw hand, foot drop, anaesthesia → trophic ulcers
Lepromatous: diffuse infiltration of skin + nasal stuffiness + 'leonine' facies
Endemic foci in DR Congo, Madagascar, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Mozambique
redFlags: Type 1 (reversal) reaction — new neuritis / nerve function deficit
Type 2 (ENL) reaction — fever, painful nodules, eye involvement

diagnostics.rationale: bacterial index — paucibacillary vs multibacillary
confirms perineural granuloma

management.detail: ≤ 5 lesions / 1 nerve: rifampicin 600 mg monthly (supervised) + dapsone 100 mg/day × 6 months.
> 5 lesions / multiple nerves / positive smear: rifampicin 600 mg monthly + clofazimine 300 mg monthly (supervised) + dapsone 100 mg/day + clofazimine 50 mg/day × 12 months.
Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day taper over 12 weeks; continue MDT.
Prednisolone ± thalidomide (specialist); clofazimine increase.
Self-care education for anaesthetic limbs + footwear + nerve function tests every 3 months during + 2 years after MDT.

title: Buruli ulcer (Mycobacterium ulcerans)
presentation: Painless nodule → induration → necrotising ulcer with undermined edges (typically lower limb)
Children 5–15 yrs in West / Central African endemic foci (Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Benin, DR Congo, Cameroon)
Often disproportionately large painless ulcer — delayed presentation common

diagnostics.rationale: definitive; lesion swab or fine-needle aspirate
support diagnosis

management.detail: Rifampicin 10 mg/kg/day + clarithromycin 7.5 mg/kg BD (or moxifloxacin 400 mg/day) × 8 weeks.
Daily dressings + debridement of necrotic tissue; skin grafting often needed for large defects.
Early mobilisation to prevent joint contractures.
WHO notifiable; national NTD programme.

title: Tetanus (clinical management)
presentation: Trismus + risus sardonicus + opisthotonos + spasms triggered by stimuli
Autonomic instability (BP swings, tachy-/brady-cardia, sweating, fever)
Neonatal tetanus — failure to suck + spasms 3–28 days after birth (umbilical contamination)
redFlags: Generalised spasms + autonomic storm (severe Ablett grade III–IV)

diagnostics.test: Clinical diagnosis — no specific lab test
diagnostics.rationale: history of wound / unimmunised + characteristic spasms

management.detail: Human tetanus immunoglobulin (HTIG) 3000–6000 IU IM single dose at site distant from wound (or equine antitoxin where HTIG unavailable, with prior skin test).
Wound debridement + metronidazole 500 mg every 8 h IV × 10 days (penicillin G acceptable alternative but may worsen spasms — GABA antagonism).
Diazepam 5–20 mg IV every 1–4 h titrated; magnesium sulphate IV 40 mg/kg load then 1–3 g/h infusion (also for autonomic storm).
Quiet darkened room. Tracheostomy + mechanical ventilation often needed for 2–4 weeks. Nutritional support + DVT prophylaxis.
Tetanus toxoid vaccine — start during recovery (disease does NOT confer immunity).

title: Burns — adult assessment + management
presentation: Erythema (superficial), blistering (partial-thickness), white/leathery painless (full-thickness)
Inhalation injury — singed nasal hair, soot in sputum, hoarseness, stridor
Circumferential burn → escharotomy needs
redFlags: TBSA > 20 % adult / 10 % child — fluid resuscitation needed
Electrical / chemical / face / hand / perineum / joint burn — refer specialist

diagnostics.rationale: estimate %TBSA (do not count erythema only)
inhalation injury
baseline + rhabdomyolysis screen (electrical)

management.detail: Intubate early if any inhalational injury — laryngeal oedema develops fast. C-spine immobilise if trauma.
100 % oxygen for CO poisoning; bronchodilator for thermal injury bronchospasm.

4 mL × kg × %TBSA Ringer's lactate over first 24 h — HALF in first 8 h from time of burn, half over next 16 h. Target urine 0.5–1 mL/kg/h. Reduce fluid if achieves target — over-resuscitation causes compartment syndrome.

Cool with running water 20 min if presented within 3 h. Cling-film cover for transfer. Tetanus prophylaxis. Avoid silver sulfadiazine on face / G6PD. Refer burns centre for TBSA > 10 % adult or any deep dermal / full-thickness.
IV opioid (morphine 0.1 mg/kg titrated); high-calorie + high-protein enteral feeding within 24 h.

title: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose
presentation: Initial 24 h — often asymptomatic or mild GI
24–72 h — right upper quadrant pain + transaminitis
72–96 h — hepatic failure: encephalopathy, coagulopathy, AKI, lactic acidosis
Staggered ingestion = ANY dose over 24 h > 75 mg/kg in adult or > 150 mg/kg in child

diagnostics.test: Paracetamol level at 4 h post ingestion (acute single overdose)
diagnostics.rationale: plot on Rumack-Matthew nomogram — 100 mg/L 'treatment line'

diagnostics.test: INR + LFTs + creatinine + bicarbonate + lactate + glucose + ABG
diagnostics.rationale: baseline + monitor for hepatic failure

diagnostics.test: Salicylate level if mixed overdose suspected
diagnostics.rationale: common co-ingestant

management.detail: Activated charcoal 1 g/kg PO/NG if within 1 h of single acute ingestion + protected airway.
Plot 4 h level on nomogram — above treatment line → IV NAC. Staggered or unknown timing → IV NAC empirically. Children weight-band dose using LBW; cap at 110 kg.
Bag 1: 150 mg/kg in 200 mL 5 % glucose over 1 h. Bag 2: 50 mg/kg in 500 mL over 4 h. Bag 3: 100 mg/kg in 1 L over 16 h. Continue beyond 21 h if INR > 1.3 / ALT rising / level still detectable.
Slow infusion + chlorphenamine 10 mg IV; do NOT permanently stop NAC.
If meeting King's College criteria (pH < 7.3, INR > 6.5, creatinine > 300, encephalopathy grade III–IV) — urgent transfer for transplant assessment.

title: Organophosphate / carbamate poisoning
presentation: SLUDGE: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI cramping, Emesis
DUMBELS: Defecation, Urination, Miosis, Bronchorrhoea/Bradycardia, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation/Sweating
Nicotinic: muscle fasciculation, weakness, paralysis (incl. respiratory)
CNS: confusion, seizures, coma
Common scenarios in SSA: pesticide self-poisoning (deliberate), agricultural exposure
redFlags: Intermediate syndrome — proximal weakness 24–96 h after acute
Suicidal ingestion — assess + plan psychiatric follow-up

diagnostics.rationale: confirms exposure + severity (RBC ChE more reliable)
baseline + pancreatitis screen
QT prolongation + bradyarrhythmia

management.detail: Staff PPE (nitrile gloves + apron + eye protection). Remove clothes + wash skin with soap + water. NG suction + activated charcoal if recent (< 1 h) oral ingestion.
1.2–3 mg IV bolus then DOUBLE every 5 min until pulmonary secretions clear + HR > 80 + SBP > 90 (often 50–100 mg cumulative). Maintain infusion at 10–20 % of loading dose per hour.
30 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV loading over 20 min then 8 mg/kg/h infusion × 18–24 h. Most effective < 24 h post exposure; less so once enzyme has 'aged'.
Diazepam 5–10 mg IV; phenobarbital if recurrent.
Intubate early if hypoxia / weakness — paralysis may last days. AVOID suxamethonium (prolonged paralysis due to suppressed pseudocholinesterase) — use rocuronium + sugammadex.
ICU observation ≥ 48 h. Psychiatric assessment before discharge if deliberate.

title: Accidental hypothermia
presentation: Mild (32–35 °C): shivering, confusion, ataxia
Moderate (28–32 °C): decreased shivering, bradycardia, J-waves on ECG, paradoxical undressing
Severe (< 28 °C): pulseless / asystole / VF, fixed pupils, apparent death
SSA contexts: night exposure at altitude, neonates without skin-to-skin, post-immersion, sepsis-induced
redFlags: Cardiac arrest with hypothermia — 'not dead until warm and dead'
Inadequate space heating / displacement / elderly living alone

diagnostics.rationale: standard digital thermometers do not read below 34 °C — Bristol or oesophageal probes required
J-waves at 32 °C; bradyarrhythmia; VF risk
lactic acidosis, hyperkalaemia, pancreatitis, DIC

management.detail: Rough movement can precipitate VF — log roll only, no chest pounding unless arrest.
Remove wet clothes, warm blankets, warm room (25 °C), sweet warm drinks if alert. Aim 0.5–2 °C/h rewarming.
Forced-air warmer (Bair Hugger) to truncal areas; warm IV fluids 40 °C; warm humidified O₂ 40 °C.
Cardiopulmonary bypass / ECMO if available — best outcome. Pleural / peritoneal / bladder lavage with warm fluid otherwise. Continue CPR + rewarming together — no death declaration until > 32 °C.
Withhold drugs < 30 °C (no clearance); thereafter double dosing intervals. Defibrillation x3 in VF — if no response, continue CPR + warm + retry at 30 °C.

title: Eclampsia
presentation: Generalised tonic-clonic seizure in patient with pre-eclampsia features (hypertension + proteinuria after 20 weeks)
Antepartum (50 %), intrapartum (25 %), postpartum (25 % — up to 6 weeks)
Often preceded by headache, visual disturbance, RUQ pain, hyper-reflexia
redFlags: HELLP syndrome (haemolysis, raised LFTs, low platelets)

diagnostics.rationale: diagnostic — sustained ≥ 140/90, severe ≥ 160/110
proteinuria ≥ 300 mg/24 h or PCR ≥ 30 mg/mmol

diagnostics.test: FBC + LFTs + creatinine + LDH + urate + clotting
diagnostics.rationale: HELLP screen

management.detail: Protect airway, oxygen, IV access ×2. Postpartum monitoring continues 24 h after delivery.

Magnesium sulphate 4 g IV over 5 min (or 5 g IM in each buttock) loading + 1 g/h IV maintenance (or 5 g IM every 4 h) — continue for 24 h after last seizure or delivery (whichever later). Monitor reflexes + RR + urine output.
Target 140–150/90–100. Labetalol 10–20 mg IV every 10 min (max 300 mg) OR hydralazine 5 mg IV every 20 min OR nifedipine 10 mg PO every 30 min.
Stabilise mother first; deliver as soon as practicable (vaginal if cervix favourable + no fetal distress; otherwise caesarean). Continue MgSO₄ 24 h postpartum.
Loss of reflexes / RR < 12 / urine < 20 mL/h — stop MgSO₄. Calcium gluconate 1 g IV slow if severe.
Continue antihypertensives postpartum until BP normalises. Multidisciplinary follow-up for cardiovascular risk.

title: Cholera
presentation: Sudden profuse painless rice-water diarrhoea + vomiting
Severe dehydration develops within hours — sunken eyes, washerwoman hands, weak pulse
May be afebrile or low-grade fever
Outbreak setting — refugee camp / flood / contaminated water

diagnostics.rationale: field diagnosis in outbreak
rapid bedside
confirmation + serotyping

management.detail: Severe dehydration (Plan C): Ringer's lactate 100 mL/kg IV — first 30 mL/kg in 30 min (60 min if < 1 yr), then 70 mL/kg in 2.5 h (5 h if < 1 yr). Reassess every 30 min. Add ORS PO 5 mL/kg/h as soon as patient can drink.
ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 h under supervision in cholera treatment centre. Continue zinc 20 mg/day × 10 days for children.
Adults: doxycycline 300 mg single dose OR azithromycin 1 g single dose. Children + pregnant: azithromycin 20 mg/kg single dose (max 1 g). Reserve for severe cases / outbreak control.
Notify district + WHO immediately. Establish cholera treatment centre. Safe water + sanitation + soap. Oral cholera vaccine (OCV) ring vaccination in coordination with district / GAVI.
Urine output target > 1 mL/kg/h; pulse + BP every 15 min; bicarbonate; glucose in children.

references.label: WHO Cholera Outbreak Response Field Manual 2024

title: Typhoid (enteric) fever
presentation: Step-ladder fever rising over 7–10 days
Relative bradycardia (Faget sign)
Hepatosplenomegaly + rose spots on trunk
Constipation early then green pea-soup diarrhoea later
Confusion + 'typhoid state' in 2nd week
redFlags: Intestinal perforation (week 3 — sudden abdominal pain + peritonism)

diagnostics.rationale: definitive — 60–80 % sensitivity
highest yield ~90 %, used when blood culture negative + clinical suspicion
low specificity in endemic areas — use only with high titres + clinical pattern

management.step: Empirical antibiotic — fluoroquinolone susceptibility falling in SSA
management.detail: Adults: azithromycin 1 g PO/IV day 1 then 500 mg/day × 6 days OR ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily × 10–14 days. Children: azithromycin 20 mg/kg/day × 7 days OR ceftriaxone 75 mg/kg/day × 10–14 days. Add carbapenem if XDR S. Typhi (Pakistan / spreading).
Paracetamol for fever. Adequate fluids. Soft diet (constipation common — avoid laxatives).
If shock / encephalopathy: dexamethasone 3 mg/kg IV then 1 mg/kg every 6 h × 48 h reduces mortality (Hoffman 1984).
Urgent surgical opinion — resection / repair. Continue broad antibiotic.
Notify. Stool culture clearance × 3 negative before food-handler return to work. Typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) for outbreaks + endemic infant immunisation (WHO SAGE 2017).

references.label: WHO Typhoid Vaccines: WHO position paper 2018

title: Ebola virus disease (EVD)
presentation: Incubation 2–21 days; presents with abrupt high fever, malaise, myalgia, headache
GI phase (day 3–10): vomiting, profuse diarrhoea, abdominal pain
Late: haemorrhagic features in some — petechiae, conjunctival haemorrhage, GI bleed
Africa endemic foci: DR Congo, Uganda, Sudan, Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia
redFlags: Travel / contact from outbreak zone within 21 days

diagnostics.rationale: single private room + PPE + dedicated equipment; notify national IHR focal point + WHO

diagnostics.test: Ebola RT-PCR on whole blood / oral swab (in ill / deceased)
diagnostics.rationale: definitive; sensitivity rises after day 3 of symptoms

diagnostics.test: Rapid antigen RDT (where PCR not available)
diagnostics.rationale: field triage in outbreak
common alternative diagnoses — never delay isolation while testing

management.detail: Single room with bathroom. Strict PPE per WHO algorithm. Cohort confirmed cases. No needle re-sheathing. Safe waste handling. Dedicated team. Restrict visitors.

Aggressive fluid replacement (oral + IV) — patients lose 5–10 L/day GI fluid. Correct electrolytes (K, Mg, Ca). Empirical antibiotics for septic shock. Antipyretic (paracetamol — AVOID aspirin/NSAIDs).
For Zaire ebolavirus: Inmazeb (atoltivimab/maftivimab/odesivimab) or Ebanga (ansuvimab) — single IV dose, 50 mg/kg per component. Substantial mortality reduction (PALM trial 2019).
rVSV-ZEBOV (Ervebo) ring vaccination of contacts + healthcare workers. Cervarix Ad26/MVA prime-boost in pre-exposure.
WHO + IHR within 24 h. Identify contacts back 21 days; monitor daily for 21 days.
Late sequelae: arthralgia, uveitis (referral), depression. Viral persistence in semen — counsel barrier contraception for ≥ 12 months.

title: Lassa fever
presentation: Insidious onset fever + malaise over 1–3 days; pharyngitis with exudate
Retrosternal pain, conjunctival injection, oedema of face/neck
Later: hearing loss (25 % of survivors), GI bleed, encephalopathy
West Africa endemic: Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Guinea (rural Mastomys natalensis rodent zones)
redFlags: Travel / contact in endemic West African zone

diagnostics.rationale: ribavirin started empirically; viral load high; transmission via body fluids

diagnostics.test: Lassa RT-PCR on serum / throat swab
diagnostics.rationale: definitive
serology

management.detail: Single room, PPE, dedicated team. Notify IHR. Less aggressive PPE than Ebola but still strict.
30 mg/kg loading IV then 16 mg/kg every 6 h × 4 days then 8 mg/kg every 8 h × 6 days. Most effective if started within 6 days of illness. Reduces mortality 5× in severe disease (McCormick 1986).
IV fluids + electrolytes. Avoid aspirin / NSAIDs (haemorrhage).
Termination of pregnancy in severe Lassa improves maternal survival (high obstetric mortality).
WHO within 24 h. Monitor contacts daily for fever × 21 days.

title: Mpox (monkeypox)
presentation: Fever + lymphadenopathy (distinguishing feature from smallpox / VZV) + headache + myalgia
Rash 1–3 days later: deep-seated firm vesiculopustules — face, palms, soles, oropharynx, anogenital
Lesions evolve synchronously through macule → papule → vesicle → pustule → crust over 2–4 weeks
Clade I (Central Africa) — historically more severe than Clade II (West Africa). 2024 SSA outbreak — Clade Ib + Ia
redFlags: Mucosal involvement causing airway / eye complications

diagnostics.rationale: definitive; swab vesicle/pustule fluid or crust
frequent co-presentation; alters severity
current outbreak transmitted often via close intimate contact

management.detail: Until all lesions crusted + new epithelialised skin (typically 2–4 weeks). Single room / cohort. Standard + contact + droplet PPE; airborne PPE during aerosol-generating procedures.
Analgesia (paracetamol, opioid if severe — rectal lesions painful). Adequate fluids. Topical antiseptic. Manage bacterial superinfection.
Tecovirimat 600 mg BD PO × 14 days (adult) — evidence for severe disease, immunocompromised, paediatric, pregnancy. Brincidofovir as alternative.
MVA-BN (Imvanex / Jynneos) — ring vaccination of contacts. Post-exposure within 4 days for prevention; up to 14 days to modify severity.
WHO + IHR (PHEIC declared August 2024). Contact tracing for 21 days.

title: Croup (laryngotracheobronchitis)
presentation: Children 6 months–6 years, peak 1–2 yr; autumn/winter peak
Coryza for 12–48 h → barking 'seal' cough + inspiratory stridor + hoarse voice
Worse at night + when distressed
Mild — stridor only on exertion / agitation
Moderate — stridor at rest + mild–moderate recession
Severe — marked stridor + recession + RR ↑ + agitation / drowsiness + cyanosis
redFlags: Drooling + leaning forward + toxic appearance → epiglottitis (do NOT examine throat)
Sudden onset without coryza → foreign body aspiration
Failure to respond to nebulised adrenaline in 30 min

diagnostics.rationale: do not perform routine bloods or imaging in mild–moderate croup

diagnostics.test: Lateral neck X-ray (only if epiglottitis differential)
diagnostics.rationale: subglottic narrowing 'steeple sign' in croup; 'thumbprint' in epiglottitis

management.detail: Sit child on parent's lap; minimise distress; do not look in throat unless prepared to manage airway.
Single dose oral dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg (or 0.6 mg/kg if moderate/severe; max 16 mg). Onset in 1–2 h. Acceptable: prednisolone 1 mg/kg as alternative. Discharge after 4 h observation if improved.
Nebulised adrenaline 5 mL of 1:1000 (5 mg) via O₂ mask — repeat in 30 min if no response. Onset minutes. Observe ≥ 4 h after (rebound effect).
Call paediatric anaesthetist. Senior airway team — small-bore endotracheal tube (1 size smaller than predicted) in theatre. IV access only AFTER airway secured.
Croup typically resolves over 3–5 days. Return if stridor at rest, working hard to breathe, drowsy, drooling, or new fever.

title: Bronchiolitis (under 2 years)
presentation: Children under 2 yrs (peak 3–6 months) with coryza progressing to cough + tachypnoea + wheeze + fine crackles
Feeding difficulty (key clinical marker)
Peak severity day 3–5 of illness, lasts 7–10 days
RSV most common; rhinovirus, hMPV, parainfluenza
redFlags: Marked respiratory distress (RR > 70, grunting, severe recession)
High-risk: < 3 months, ex-preterm, congenital heart disease, CLD, neuromuscular disease, immunocompromised

diagnostics.rationale: RSV PCR only for cohorting purposes when admitted

diagnostics.test: CXR + bloods only if uncertain diagnosis or critical
diagnostics.rationale: avoid unnecessary investigations — diffuse hyperinflation + atelectasis on CXR

management.detail: Maintain oxygen saturation ≥ 92 % (consider lower threshold in well-perfused infants per NICE). High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) for moderate-severe. NG / IV fluids if poor feeding (give 2/3 maintenance to avoid SIADH). Avoid sedation.
Routine bronchodilators (salbutamol, ipratropium), corticosteroids, antibiotics, hypertonic saline, ribavirin, chest physiotherapy — NOT recommended in typical bronchiolitis.
Consider HFNC 2 L/kg/min, CPAP, intubation for type 2 RF / exhaustion. RSV monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab) for prevention in high-risk infants.
Safe to discharge when feeding adequately (> 50–75 %), SpO₂ ≥ 92 % on air for several hours, parents confident. Safety-net advice on red flags.

title: Cervical cancer screening (HPV/VIA/cytology)
presentation: Screening of asymptomatic women — most early lesions silent
Risk amplified by HIV, smoking, multiple partners, lack of prior screening
Cervical cancer leading cause of cancer death in women in SSA
redFlags: Postmenopausal bleeding — refer for colposcopy regardless of screening result

diagnostics.rationale: WHO preferred — every 5 years from age 30 (or 25 if HIV+); higher sensitivity than VIA / cytology
single-visit screen-and-treat — practical in low-resource settings; every 3 years from 25–49
where HPV testing unavailable; every 3 years 25–49 + every 5 years 50–65

management.detail: Recall at 5 yrs (HPV) or 3 yrs (VIA/cytology). HIV+ women — recall at 3 yrs (HPV) or annually (VIA/cytology).

management.step: HPV positive — partial genotyping (16/18 +) or VIA / cytology abnormal
management.detail: Triage with colposcopy + biopsy. If cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN2/3) — excisional treatment (LLETZ / cone biopsy).
VIA-positive + acetowhite lesion eligible for thermal ablation / cryotherapy → same-visit treatment. Refer if lesion > 75 % of cervix, extends into endocervix, or suspicion of invasion.
HPV vaccination programme — single dose for girls 9–14 (WHO SAGE 2022). Address HIV control + smoking cessation.

title: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
presentation: Sudden severe unilateral eye pain + headache + nausea / vomiting
Red eye with cloudy / 'steamy' cornea + fixed mid-dilated pupil
Halos around lights + visual loss
Risk factors: hyperopia, age > 50, Asian ethnicity, dim light, anticholinergic drugs (TCA, antihistamine, atropine)
redFlags: Failure to respond to medical therapy within 1 h

diagnostics.rationale: diagnostic — IOP > 30 mmHg (often > 50)
shallow anterior chamber + closed angle

management.detail: Send to eye unit immediately; vision-threatening.
Lie patient supine. Topical drops: timolol 0.5 % one drop + apraclonidine 1 % + pilocarpine 2 % every 5 min × 3. Systemic: acetazolamide 500 mg IV (or 500 mg PO) then 250 mg every 6 h.

management.step: If IOP > 50 or unresponsive at 1 h
management.detail: IV mannitol 1–2 g/kg over 30 min (caution in cardiac / renal disease). Topical steroid (dexamethasone) once IOP starts falling.
Peripheral iridotomy bilaterally (other eye is at risk) within 24–48 h once cornea clears.
Avoid anticholinergic drugs. Counsel re recurrence in untreated fellow eye.

title: Testicular torsion
presentation: Sudden severe unilateral scrotal pain + swelling (often during sleep or sport)
Nausea + vomiting
Peak age — neonatal + adolescent (10–18 yrs)
High-riding testis with horizontal lie + absent cremasteric reflex
redFlags: Time from onset > 6 h — testicular viability dropping rapidly
Bilateral pain (perinatal torsion → both can twist)
Suspected intermittent torsion (recurrent episodes — refer for elective fixation)

diagnostics.test: Clinical diagnosis — DO NOT DELAY for imaging
diagnostics.rationale: TWIST score (testicular swelling, hard testis, absent cremasteric reflex, nausea/vomiting, high-riding) — high score → straight to theatre

diagnostics.test: Doppler ultrasound only if equivocal + immediately available
diagnostics.rationale: absent intratesticular flow; never delay surgery > 30 min for imaging
